questions.question: What happens if you lose air pressure in the emergency line?
questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve closes.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the trailer's brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks. Losing air pressure in the emergency line causes the valve to close and activates the emergency trailer brakes.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never try to beat a train across the tracks.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach a railroad crossing. You may not hear a train coming, and signals might not warn you in time. Never try to outdrive a train at a railroad crossing.

questions.question: How can you tell if a converter dolly has ABS?

options.text: By a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.
By a blue lamp on the left side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: By a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.
questions.explanation: Dollies made after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). A dolly with ABS has a yellow lamp on its left side.

questions.question: Why are roads extra slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel washes to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not made for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first begins. Fresh rainwater mixes with oil and grease on the road to create a slick film. As more rain falls, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control the vehicle better while turning.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires from the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for the ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.

questions.question: Which surface has the least traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Be very careful when driving on melting ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: When do large combination vehicles take the longest to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: When empty.
questions.explanation: Large combination vehicles take longer to stop when empty than when loaded. Less weight means the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: Which is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful near people who are not paying attention to traffic. Watch out for road workers, drivers talking to passengers, and children near the road.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs replacing
Because compressed air contains water that must be drained
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be drained
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What are passive railroad crossings?

options.text: They have no traffic control devices.
They have gates that lower when trains approach.
Commercial vehicles should never cross them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have no traffic control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: How should you position the tractor when backing up to couple a trailer?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle in front of the trailer.
Straight in front of the trailer.
At a 30-degree angle in front of the trailer.
At a 60-degree angle in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor straight in front of the trailer. Backing at an angle can damage the landing gear and cause the trailer to move.

questions.question: What should not happen to air lines during a coupling inspection?

options.text: They are not connected to the glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are leaking.
questions.explanation: Air lines must be securely attached to the glad hands with no leaks. They should have enough slack to allow easy turning.

questions.question: How can you check if a road is becoming icy?

options.text: Open the window and check the mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and check the mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: Open your window and feel the side mirror or antenna. If ice has formed on these parts, the road is likely becoming icy.

questions.question: Which is NOT an example of a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver operating a vehicle with ice on the windshield.
The operator of a rental truck.
A driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows.
A person operating a pick-up truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck.
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. Examples include those with ice on the windshield, those with items blocking windows, and those driving rental trucks they are not familiar with.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor.
questions.explanation: Both systems share one air compressor. If it fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the drinks were consumed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The temperature of the drinks.
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the person's weight.

questions.question: What happens to your speed when traveling down a hill?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your speed increases.
questions.explanation: Gravity causes your speed to increase when going downhill.

questions.question: What can cause poisonous fumes to enter the cab?

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: A defective exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A damaged exhaust system is dangerous because it allows poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you plan to slow down?

options.text: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before braking.
Turn on one set of turn signals.
Put your hand out the window and wave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before braking.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap the brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This warns drivers behind you that you are about to slow down.
